claim: Staphylococcus aureus pathogenicity islands (SaPIs) are clinically important mobile genetic elements.
source: Remarkably, the clinically important Staphylococcus aureus pathogenicity islands (SaPIs) use this tactic to spread in nature.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a characterization of SaPIs

claim: SaPIs reside passively in the host chromosome under the control of the SaPI-encoded master repressor, Stl.
source: SaPIs reside passively in the host chromosome, under the control of the SaPI-encoded master repressor, Stl.
evidence: Direct statement in the abstract describing SaPI behavior

claim: SaPI de-repression is effected by specific phage proteins that bind to Stl, initiating the SaPI cycle.
source: It has been assumed that SaPI de-repression is effected by specific phage proteins that bind to Stl, initiating the SaPI cycle.
evidence: Statement in abstract describing the mechanism of SaPI activation

claim: Different SaPIs encode different Stl repressors.
source: Different SaPIs encode different Stl repressors, so each targets a specific phage protein for its de-repression.
evidence: Direct statement in abstract about SaPI diversity

claim: SaPI Stl repressors have acquired different domains to interact with unrelated proteins encoded by different phages.
source: This is accomplished because the SaPI Stl repressors have acquired different domains to interact with unrelated proteins, encoded by different phages, but in all cases performing the same conserved function.
evidence: Main finding stated in the abstract

claim: The unrelated phage proteins that interact with Stl repressors all perform the same conserved function.
source: This is accomplished because the SaPI Stl repressors have acquired different domains to interact with unrelated proteins, encoded by different phages, but in all cases performing the same conserved function.

claim: This strategy allows intra- and inter-generic SaPI transfer.
source: This elegant strategy allows intra- and inter-generic SaPI transfer, highlighting these elements as one of nature's most fascinating subcellular parasites.

claim: SaPIs carry and disseminate superantigen genes, especially those for toxic shock toxin and enterotoxin B.
source: The SaPIs are clinically relevant because they carry and disseminate superantigen genes, especially those for toxic shock toxin and enterotoxin B.
evidence: Direct statement about SaPI clinical relevance in introduction

claim: SaPIs are exclusively responsible for menstrual toxic shock.
source: They are very widespread among the staphylococci and are exclusively responsible for menstrual toxic shock, a rare but important human disease.
evidence: Direct statement in introduction about disease causation

claim: Stl is a DNA-binding protein whose sequence is rather poorly conserved among different members of the SaPI family.
source: In the absence of a helper phage they reside passively in the host chromosome, under the control of a global SaPI-coded repressor, Stl, a DNA-binding protein whose sequence is rather poorly conserved among the different members of the SaPI family (Tormo-Más et al., 2010).

claim: Following infection by a helper phage or induction of a helper prophage, SaPIs excise, replicate extensively, and are packaged in phage-like particles.
source: Following infection by a helper phage or induction of a helper prophage, they excise, replicate extensively, and are packaged in phage-like particles composed of phage virion proteins, leading to very high frequencies of inter- as well as intrageneric transfer (Novick et al., 2010; Penadés and Christie, 2015).

claim: SaPI de-repression is effected by specific phage proteins that bind to Stl, disrupting the Stl-DNA complex.
source: In previous work we demonstrated that SaPI de-repression is effected by specific phage proteins that bind to Stl, disrupting the Stl-DNA complex and thereby initiating the excision-replication-packaging (ERP) cycle of the islands (Tormo-Más et al., 2010).
evidence: Statement of previous findings with citation

claim: The inducers for SaPIbov1, SaPIbov2 and SaPI1 correspond to the phage trimeric dUTPase (Dut), 80α ORF15 and Sri, respectively.
source: Thus, the inducers for SaPIbov1, SaPIbov2 and SaPI1 correspond to the phage trimeric dUTPase (Dut), 80α ORF15 and Sri, respectively (Tormo-Más et al., 2010, 2013).

claim: SaPIs require phage proteins to be packaged.
source: Since SaPIs require phage proteins to be packaged, this strategy couples the SaPI and phage cycles, but imposes a significant transmission cost on the helper phages (Frígols et al., 2015).

claim: Phages carrying mutations in genes encoding SaPI inducers have a fitness cost when competing with wild-type phages.
source: Importantly, although phages carrying mutations in the genes encoding the aforementioned SaPI inducers can be propagated in the lab, these mutations have a fitness cost when the mutant phages compete with the wild-type phages in the same conditions (Frígols et al., 2015), which indicates that the phage coded SaPI inducers provide an important function for the phages in nature.

claim: All staphylococcal S. aureus phages encode Duts; some encode dimeric and others trimeric Duts, never both.
source: While all the staphylococcal S. aureus phages encode Duts; some encode dimeric and others trimeric Duts, never both (Frígols et al., 2015).

claim: Dimeric and trimeric Duts are completely unrelated both in sequence and structure, representing a nice example of convergent evolution.
source: Importantly, dimeric and trimeric Duts are completely unrelated both in sequence and structure, representing a nice example of convergent evolution (Penadés et al., 2013).

claim: The trimeric Duts from phages 80α and ϕ11 were initially described as the SaPIbov1 inducers.
source: While the 80α and ϕ11 phage-encoded trimeric Duts were initially described as the SaPIbov1 inducers (Tormo-Más et al., 2010; 2013), the dimeric Dut from phage ϕNM1 also induces SaPIbov1 (Hill and Dokland, 2016; Hill et al., 2017).

claim: The dimeric Dut from phage ϕNM1 also induces SaPIbov1.
source: While the 80α and ϕ11 phage-encoded trimeric Duts were initially described as the SaPIbov1 inducers (Tormo-Más et al., 2010; 2013), the dimeric Dut from phage ϕNM1 also induces SaPIbov1 (Hill and Dokland, 2016; Hill et al., 2017).

claim: The ϕO11 dimeric Dut induces the SaPIbov1 and SaPIbov5 cycles.
source: Interestingly, the ϕO11 dimeric Dut also induces the SaPIbov1 and SaPIbov5 cycles (Figure 1A).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to experimental data in Figure 1A

claim: Expression of the ϕO11 dimeric Dut induced SaPIbov1 and SaPIbov5 excision and replication.
source: Thus, when overexpressed, the cloned ϕO11 dimeric dut induced SaPIbov1 and SaPIbov5 excision and replication (Figure 1A).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 1A showing experimental results

claim: The structure of the phage 80α and ϕ11 coded Duts has recently been solved.
source: The structure of the phage 80α and ϕ11 coded Duts has recently been solved (Leveles et al., 2013; Tormo-Más et al., 2013).

claim: The trimeric Dut domains IV, V and VI are involved in SaPIbov1 Stl recognition.
source: Moreover, in-depth structural, genetic and biochemical studies have demonstrated that the trimeric Dut domains IV, V and VI are involved in SaPIbov1 Stl recognition (Maiques et al., 2016; Tormo-Más et al., 2010, 2013).

claim: The dimeric ϕNM1 and ϕO11 Duts are basically identical except in a divergent central region.
source: As occurred with the trimeric Duts (Tormo-Más et al., 2010), the dimeric ϕNM1 and ϕO11 Duts are basically identical except in a divergent central region (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Statement with reference to figure supplement showing sequence comparison

claim: SaPIbov5 encodes the same Stl repressor as SaPIbov1.
source: Note that SaPIbov5 was also included in these studies because it encodes the same Stl repressor as SaPIbov1, with both islands being induced by the same helper phages (Carpena et al., 2016; Viana et al., 2010).

claim: Induction of ϕO11 dut strongly increased β-lactamase expression from the str promoter.
source: Induction of ϕO11 dut strongly increased β-lactamase expression from the str promoter (Figure 1B).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to experimental data in Figure 1B

claim: It was possible to co-purify a complex between His6-StlSaPIbov1 and ϕO11 Dut.
source: It was possible to co-purify a complex between His6-StlSaPIbov1 and ϕO11 Dut (Figure 1C).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to experimental data in Figure 1C

claim: Dimeric ϕO11 Dut induces the SaPI cycle using the same mechanism described for the unrelated trimeric Dut proteins.
source: We conclude from these results that dimeric ϕO11 Dut induces the SaPI cycle using the same mechanism described for the unrelated trimeric Dut proteins.

claim: The structure of the dimeric ϕO11 Dut in complex with the nonhydrolyzable dUTP analog α,β-imido-dUTP (dUPNPP) and Mg2+ was determined at 2.1 Å resolution.
source: To test this hypothesis, and since the structure of the staphylococcal phage-encoded dimeric Duts remains unsolved, the structure of the dimeric ϕO11 Dut in complex with the nonhydrolyzable dUTP analog α,β-imido-dUTP (dUPNPP) and Mg2+ was determined at 2.1 Å resolution (Supplementary file 1).

claim: The crystal structure showed 2 molecules in the asymmetric unit organized as a homodimer.
source: The crystal structure showed 2 molecules in the asymmetric unit organized as a homodimer (Figure 2).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 2

claim: ϕO11 is an all-helix protein composed of only seven α-helices per protomer.
source: The structure shows that ϕO11 is an all-helix protein composed of only seven α-helices (α1, residues 7–23; α2, 29–47; α3 61–82; α4, 86–98; α5, 104–108; α6, 110–121 and α7, 127–141) per protomer.

claim: The ϕO11 dimeric Dut has a 'compact' conformation compared to counterparts in other organisms.
source: Interestingly, the ϕO11 dimeric Dut has a 'compact' conformation compared to counterparts in other organisms (which encompass ten or more α-helices) (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figures

claim: None of the motifs IV, V and VI present in trimeric Duts are present in the ϕO11 Dut.
source: As could be anticipated by the difference in folding between the trimeric (all-beta) and dimeric (all-alpha) proteins, none of these motifs are present in the ϕO11 Dut (Figures 2 and 3).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to figures

claim: The active centres in trimeric and dimeric Duts show divergent architecture.
source: Therefore, the active centres in both types of enzymes show divergent architecture and, consequently, the spatial disposition of the residues surrounding the nucleotides, including those provided by motif IV, V and VI, is completely different.

claim: The SaPIbov1 Stl repressor has different interacting domains/ways to recognise the unrelated trimeric and dimeric Duts.
source: Taken together, these results strongly suggest that the SaPIbov1 Stl repressor has different interacting domains/ways to recognise the unrelated trimeric and dimeric Duts.

claim: The elimination of the C-terminal subdomain impairs the binding to the dimeric but not to the trimeric Dut.
source: Conversely, the elimination of the C-terminal subdomain impairs the binding to the dimeric but not to the trimeric Dut (Figure 4A).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 4A

claim: The interaction with the Stl repressor inhibits the dUTPase activity of both dimeric and trimeric Duts.
source: Moreover, it has been shown the interaction with the Stl repressor inhibits the dUTPase activity of both dimeric and trimeric Duts (Hill and Dokland, 2016; Szabó et al., 2014).

claim: StlΔHTH inhibits the dUTPase activity of dimeric but not trimeric Duts.
source: Furthermore, and in agreement with the binding capacity shown by the Stl deletional variants, StlΔHTH inhibits the dUTPase activity of dimeric but not trimeric Duts, while StlΔCter has the opposite capacity (Figure 4B).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 4B

claim: StlΔCter inhibits the dUTPase activity of trimeric but not dimeric Duts.
source: Furthermore, and in agreement with the binding capacity shown by the Stl deletional variants, StlΔHTH inhibits the dUTPase activity of dimeric but not trimeric Duts, while StlΔCter has the opposite capacity (Figure 4B).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 4B

claim: A single spontaneous 80α phage mutant was obtained which was able to form plaques on S. aureus strain RN4220 containing SaPI2.
source: After many attempts, we obtained only a single spontaneous 80α phage mutant which was able to form plaques on S. aureus strain RN4220 containing SaPI2, suggesting that the SaPI2 inducer is absolutely essential for the phage cycle even in laboratory conditions.

claim: In the 80α mutant phage, the 3' region of the 80α ORF16 has been lost.
source: In this mutant the 3' region of the 80α ORF16 has been lost.

claim: The 80α ORF16 protein belongs to the Sak family of single strand annealing proteins (SSAP, also called recombinases) involved in homologous recombination.
source: The 80α ORF16 protein belongs to the Sak family of single strand annealing proteins (SSAP, also called recombinases) involved in homologous recombination (Lopes et al., 2010; Scaltriti et al., 2011).

claim: The 80α ORF16 protein is essential for 80α phage replication.
source: Although for many of these proteins their role in the phage cycle has not been established yet, we have recently demonstrated that this protein is essential for 80α phage replication (Neamah et al., 2017).

claim: The cloned sak (but not the chimeric Sak-Ssb protein) induced SaPI2 excision and replication when overexpressed.
source: Thus, when overexpressed, the cloned sak (but not the chimeric Sak-Ssb protein) induced SaPI2 excision and replication (Figure 5).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 5

claim: Induction of sak, but not the chimeric sak-ssb, strongly increased β-lactamase expression from the str promoter.
source: Induction of sak, but not the chimeric sak-ssb, strongly increased β-lactamase expression from the str promoter (Figure 6A).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 6A

claim: It was possible to co-purify a complex between His6-StlSaPI2 and Sak.
source: It was possible to co-purify a complex between His6-StlSaPI2 and Sak (Figure 6B), whereas untagged Sak alone did not bind to the resin.
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 6B

claim: The chimeric Sak-Ssb did not co-purify with His6-StlSaPI2.
source: The chimeric Sak-Ssb, which does not derepress SaPI2 (Figure 6A), did not co-purify with His6-StlSaPI2, confirming the specificity of the His6-StlSaPI2::Sak interaction.
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 6A

claim: Phages ϕ80 and ϕ52A can also induce the SaPI2 cycle.
source: Interestingly, phages ϕ80 and ϕ52A can also induce the SaPI2 cycle (Ram et al., 2014), although none of them encodes a 80α Sak protein.

claim: Both ϕ80 and ϕ52A phages carried an identical gene encoding a protein that belongs to the Sak4 family of SSAPs.
source: Both ϕ80 and ϕ52A phages carried an identical gene, named ORF13 in phage ϕ80 and ORF16 in phage ϕ52A, which encodes a non-related protein to the 80α Sak (Figure 5—figure supplement 3). This protein belongs to a distinct family of SSAPs, Sak4 (Lopes et al., 2010).
evidence: Direct statement with citation and reference to figure

claim: Sak4 and Sak are both SSAPs (recombinases) performing a similar function in their cognate phages.
source: While Sak4 and Sak are not homologous in sequence (Figure 5—figure supplement 3), we have recently demonstrated that they are both SSAPs (recombinases) performing a similar function in their cognate phages (Neamah et al., 2017).
evidence: Statement with citation and reference to figure

claim: Expression of the ϕ80 and ϕ52A Sak4 proteins in a SaPI2 positive strain demonstrated that they are sufficient to induce the SaPI2 cycle.
source: Thus, expression of the ϕ80 and ϕ52A Sak4 proteins in a SaPI2 positive strain demonstrated that they are sufficient to induce the SaPI2 cycle (Figure 5).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 5

claim: Expression of the sak4 genes strongly increased β-lactamase expression from the Stl-repressed str promoter.
source: Moreover, expression of the sak4 genes strongly increased β-lactamase expression from the Stl-repressed str promoter (Figure 6A).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 6A

claim: A two-hybrid assay confirmed the strong interaction between the ϕ52A Sak4 recombinase and the SaPI2 Stl repressor.
source: However, a two-hybrid assay confirmed the strong interaction between both the ϕ52A Sak4 recombinase and the SaPI2 Stl repressor and between the 80α Sak protein and the SaPI2 Stl pair (used here as a control; Figure 6C), confirming that the phage Sak4 protein is a bona fide SaPI2 inducer.
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 6C

claim: Staphylococcal phages encode at least 4 distant SSAP families, including Erf, Redβ, Sak and Sak4.
source: In silico scrutiny looking at the genes located upstream of the ssb genes revealed that staphylococcal phages encode at least 4 distant SSAP families, including Erf, Redβ, and the aforementioned Sak and Sak4 (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: Direct statement from in silico analysis

claim: All the staphylococcal phages encode one SSAP.
source: All the staphylococcal phages encode one SSAP, in accordance with the fact that these proteins are essential for the phage (Neamah et al., 2017).

claim: The expression of the ϕSLT Erf and ϕN315 Redβ proteins is sufficient to induce the SaPI2 cycle.
source: Applying the same methodology and strategies previously used to characterise Sak and Sak4, our results confirm that: (i) the expression of the ϕSLT Erf and ϕN315 Redβ proteins is sufficient to induce the SaPI2 cycle (Figure 5);
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 5

claim: Expression of the Erf and Redβ recombinases prevents Stl from binding to the SaPI2 stl-str divergent region.
source: (ii) expression of these recombinases prevents Stl from binding to the SaPI2 stl-str divergent region (Figure 6A)
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 6A

claim: The two-hybrid assay confirmed the interaction between the SaPI2 Stl repressor and the Erf and Redβ recombinases.
source: and (iii) the two-hybrid assay confirmed the interaction between the SaPI2 Stl repressor and the Erf and Redβ recombinases (Figure 6C).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 6C

claim: Structure-based modelling of Sak, Sak4, Erf and Redβ suggested they are unrelated.
source: Structure-based modelling of Sak, Sak4, Erf and Redβ suggested they are unrelated, although Sak, Erf and Redβ can be connected through remote homology relationships (Lopes et al., 2010).
evidence: Statement from modeling analysis with citation

claim: Sak, Erf and Redβ belong to a large superfamily adopting a shortcut Rad52-like fold.
source: Thus, it has been proposed that Sak, Erf and Redβ belong to a large superfamily adopting a shortcut Rad52-like fold (Lopes et al., 2010).

claim: Remote homologs to Sak4 are predicted to adopt a shortcut Rad51/RecA fold.
source: By contrast, remote homologs to Sak4 are predicted to adopt a shortcut Rad51/RecA fold (Lopes et al., 2010) and models obtained from I-Tasser and Phyre2 servers proposed this fold for the ϕ52A Sak4 recombinase with good confidence (Figure 7 and Supplementary files 4A and B).
evidence: Statement with citation and reference to modeling results

claim: Different SaPIbov1 Stl homologs were identified in PICI elements present in S. aureus, S. hominis, S. haemolyticus, S. lugdunensis, S. saprophyticus and S. simulans.
source: Different SaPIbov1 Stl homologs were identified in PICI elements present in S. aureus, Staphylococcus hominis, Staphylococcus haemolyticus, Staphylococcus lugdunensis, Staphylococcus saprophyticus and Staphylococcus simulans.

claim: SaPI2 Stl homologs were identified in many different Staphylococci, including S. argenteus, S. caprae, S. lugdunensis, S. epidermidis, S. haemolyticus, S. simulans, S. xylosus and S. capitis, as well as in PICI from other Gram-positive bacteria, including Bacillus decisifrondis or Streptococcus pyogenes.
source: SaPI2 Stl homologs were also identified in many different Staphylococci, including Staphylococcus argenteus, Staphylococcus caprae, S. lugdunensis, Staphylococcus epidermidis, S. haemolyticus, S. simulans, Staphylococcus xylosus and Staphylococcus capitis, as well as in PICI from other Gram-positive bacteria, including Bacillus decisifrondis or Streptococcus pyogenes.

claim: Some islands present in different species encode identical Stl repressors, suggesting inter-species transfer.
source: Of note is the fact that some islands, present in different species, encode identical Stl repressors, suggesting inter-species transfer.

claim: Both the dimeric ϕO11 and trimeric ϕ11 Duts induced β-lactamase expression from the Stl-repressed str promoters present in the ShoCI794_SEPI and ShaCI51-48 islands.
source: Remarkably, both the dimeric ϕO11 and trimeric ϕ11 Duts induced β-lactamase expression from the Stl-repressed str promoters present in the ShoCI794_SEPI and ShaCI51-48 islands (Table 1), suggesting that the Stl repressors encoded in all these islands have a common origin.
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Table 1

claim: The 80α coded Sak induced SaPI2, SeCINIHLM095 and ShaCI137133, but not ScCIUMC-CNS-990.
source: Thus, the 80α coded Sak induced SaPI2, SeCINIHLM095 and ShaCI137133, but not ScCIUMC-CNS-990 (Table 2).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Table 2

claim: The chimeric 80α Sak-Ssb protein induced none of the tested islands.
source: The chimeric 80α Sak-Ssb protein induced none, supporting that the different PICI coded Stl repressors are structurally related (Table 2).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Table 2

claim: The ϕ52A coded Sak4 recombinase induced SaPI2 and ScCIUMC-CNS-990.
source: Interestingly, the ϕ52A coded Sak4 recombinase induced SaPI2 and ScCIUMC-CNS-990, while the ϕSLT Erf recombinase induced SaPI2 and SeCINIHLM095.

claim: The ϕSLT Erf recombinase induced SaPI2 and SeCINIHLM095.
source: Interestingly, the ϕ52A coded Sak4 recombinase induced SaPI2 and ScCIUMC-CNS-990, while the ϕSLT Erf recombinase induced SaPI2 and SeCINIHLM095.

claim: The ϕN315 coded Redβ recombinase uniquely induced SaPI2, but not the other islands.
source: Finally, the ϕN315 coded Redβ recombinase uniquely induced SaPI2, but not the other islands (Table 2).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Table 2

claim: Homologs to the SaPIbov1 or SaPI2 inducer were identified in all the analysed phages infecting species other than S. aureus.
source: As shown in Supplementary file 6, we were able to identify homologs to the previously characterised SaPIbov1 or SaPI2 inducer in all the analysed phages, although with different degrees of identity among the members of the distinct families.

claim: The behaviour of the S. epidermidis IPLA6 trimeric Dut was identical to that observed for the trimeric ϕ11 Dut.
source: That was the case, and the behaviour of the S. epidermidis IPLA6 trimeric Dut was identical to that observed for the trimeric ϕ11 Dut (Table 1), while the functioning of the ϕPH15 Sak recombinase was indistinguishable from that observed with the homologue S. aureus 80α coded Sak (Table 2).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Table 1

claim: The functioning of the ϕPH15 Sak recombinase was indistinguishable from that observed with the homologue S. aureus 80α coded Sak.
source: That was the case, and the behaviour of the S. epidermidis IPLA6 trimeric Dut was identical to that observed for the trimeric ϕ11 Dut (Table 1), while the functioning of the ϕPH15 Sak recombinase was indistinguishable from that observed with the homologue S. aureus 80α coded Sak (Table 2).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Table 2

claim: The ScCIM23864:W1 (S. caprae) and SlCIFDAARGOS_141 (S. lugdunensis) elements are identical (just 3 mismatches over 13,847 nt).
source: Highlighting the versatility of these elements and the successful strategy they use to spread in nature, our analysis revealed that the ScCIM23864:W1 (S. caprae) and SlCIFDAARGOS_141 (S. lugdunensis) elements are identical (just 3 mismatches over 13,847 nt; Supplementary file 7).

claim: The most likely scenario explaining why the SaPI/PICI Stl repressors can interact with different phage coded inducers is the existence of different interacting domains in the SaPI Stl repressors.
source: Our results suggest that the most likely scenario explaining why the SaPI/PICI Stl repressors can interact with different phage coded inducers is the existence of different interacting domains in the SaPI Stl repressors.

claim: The presence of different domains in Stl repressors highlights the co-evolutionary and constant battle established between the helper phages and the parasitic PICIs.
source: The presence of these different domains highlights the co-evolutionary and constant battle established between the helper phages, trying to avoid PICIs induction, and the parasitic PICIs, trying to interact with non-inducing phages (Frígols et al., 2015).

claim: The fact that the Stl repressors interact with structurally unrelated proteins performing the same function makes this strategy unique in nature and extremely effective.
source: The fact that the Stl repressors interact with structurally unrelated proteins performing the same function makes this strategy unique in nature and extremely effective.

claim: By targeting conserved phage processes, the fact that the SaPIs target different versions of proteins involved in the same biological processes limits the capacity of the phages to overcome SaPI parasitism.
source: By contrast, and since the processes targeted by the SaPIs are extremely well conserved in the staphylococcal phages, the fact that the SaPIs target different versions of proteins involved in the same biological processes limits the capacity of the phages to overcome SaPI parasitism, ensuring the transferability of these elements.

claim: SaPI-phage interactions represent a remarkable microcosm within the bacterial intracellular universe.
source: Thus, our results show that SaPI-phage interactions represent a remarkable microcosm within the bacterial intracellular universe, highlighting SaPIs as one of the most fascinating and effective subcellular parasites.

claim: The proteins targeted by the AbiK system are the different phage encoded SSAPs involved in homologous recombination.
source: As occurs with SaPI2, the proteins targeted by the AbiK system are the different phage encoded SSAPs involved in homologous recombination (Bouchard and Moineau, 2004).

claim: The mechanism by which AbiK blocks phage reproduction does not seem to involve the formation of a complex between the AbiK protein and the recombinases.
source: Although the mechanism by which AbiK blocks phage reproduction remains unclear, it does not seem to involve the formation of a complex between the AbiK protein and the recombinases, as occurs with SaPI2 (Bouchard and Moineau, 2004; Wang et al., 2011).
